content:
{'translated': 'Pebblebee has launched the "LÔC8," a distinctive Android Find Hub / Apple Find My tracker designed to be hidden inside your bike handlebar, golf club, or other places, so you can keep track of your belongings at any time.'}

{'translated': 'In addition to Pebblebee\'s other wide range of trackers, the "LÔC8" is custom-made and can be installed in places you wouldn\'t expect. This cylindrical tracker\'s main targets are bikes and golf clubs, but theoretically you can put it inside any "stick-shaped" object. However, its design is clearly meant to be embedded inside an object rather than used on its own.'}

{'translated': 'The "LÔC8" features a transparent plastic shell and is not designed to be used exposed. But strictly speaking, if you simply toss it into a pocket in your backpack or suitcase, it will still work, and the performance should be quite decent, since Pebblebee boasts a 3-year battery life and "uncompromising performance." The caveat is that the battery must not shift out of place, since it\'s directly exposed inside the tube body.'}

{'translated': "The battery is not rechargeable, but it is replaceable. At least that's what Pebblebee says. I briefly looked it up, and the ER10250 battery used inside seems hard to find online, so replacing the battery won't be as simple as swapping out a coin cell."}

{'translated': "However, the overall usage process is quite simple—certainly much easier than removing the grips from my bike's handlebars (you might be curious—a quick spray of WD-40 will do the trick)."}

{'translated': "The top of the tracker serves as a button; a double-tap activates pairing mode. Then simply use a nearby phone to connect to Android Find Hub (or iPhone Find My), place the tracker inside your bike, golf club, or wherever else you want to install it, and you're done. Two different-sized sleeves are included in the box to fit various bike handlebars, though for now it's mainly targeted at mountain bikes. You can then refit the regular handlebar grips as normal. The battery lasts three years, and if the tip of the tracker is still exposed, you'll see the LED light up when you locate it using the Find Hub app."}

{'translated': 'The concept is simple yet clever, but the potential is enormous. Bike theft is extremely common in urban areas, and while installing an AirTag-like tracker isn\'t exactly difficult, a design like the "LÔC8" gives thieves virtually no way to tamper with it. As for golf clubs, there\'s simply no other option besides this one. It\'s truly delightful to see such an elegant solution finally come to market. Pebblebee revealed this plan to us as early as early 2025, and they have even more ideas in the pipeline, including a "thin" tracker that can be embedded in items like snowboards.'}

{'translated': 'Pebblebee is selling the "LÔC8" in 1-packs and 4-packs, with the former priced at USD 39.99, mainly targeting general users who want to DIY the installation on their own gear. The 4-pack is designed specifically for golf club sets and is installed by professionals.'}
